title: Does a range expansion enrich the swim kind of c45's Marangoni ladder at the colonizing front (spatial sorting), and does the enrichment decay once the box is full?
summary: Spatial sorting (Shine et al. 2011) selects dispersal by arrival rather than survival: fast kinds reach empty space first and reproduce there. Perkins et al. 2016 predict lasting enrichment after expansion only without a dispersal/division trade-off; c45's screen shows swimming costs divisions in the Marangoni rods, so the prediction is a front enrichment that decays. The ladder world already breeds three kinds true (mar 20/40/60) and has an identical-event twin.
experiment: world.py of 20261026T2018-c45-marangoni-ladder with its ancestors seeded only in a strip of width 1/4 box (the rest bath-filled, nothing else changed), 2 seeds, run until the box is full plus as long again. Measure the share of the mar-60 kind (and of dividing rods that swim 3 of their own lengths) in the front decile versus the core over time, against the identical-event twin (every body at the ancestral mar) and the same strip start with the drive off. Enrichment at the front that the twin lacks is spatial sorting; its fate after filling tests the trade-off.
